title: GitLab CI/CD — Pipelines & Caching
summary: GitLab CI is declarative YAML, but writing pipelines that are fast, reliable, and maintainable requires knowing the gotchas around job ordering, caching, artifacts, and variable precedence. This lesson covers the patterns you'll use in production IaC pipelines.

sections.title: Pipeline anatomy — stages, jobs, rules
sections.body:
```yaml
# .gitlab-ci.yml

# Stages run in order. Jobs in the same stage run in parallel.
stages:
  - validate
  - plan
  - apply
  - notify

# Default settings applied to all jobs unless overridden
default:
  image: python:3.12-slim
  before_script:
    - pip install -r requirements.txt --quiet
  retry:
    max: 2
    when:
      - runner_system_failure
      - stuck_or_timeout_failure

# Variables available to all jobs
variables:
  AWS_DEFAULT_REGION: eu-central-1
  TF_VERSION: "1.8.0"
  DOCKER_DRIVER: overlay2

# A concrete job
tf-validate:
  stage: validate
  image: hashicorp/terraform:${TF_VERSION}
  script:
    - terraform init -backend=false
    - terraform validate
    - terraform fmt -check
  rules:
    # Only run on MRs and main branch, not tags
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH

tf-plan:
  stage: plan
  image: hashicorp/terraform:${TF_VERSION}
  script:
    - terraform init
    - terraform plan -out=tfplan
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - tfplan
      - .terraform.lock.hcl
    expire_in: 1 day
  environment:
    name: production
    action: prepare

tf-apply:
  stage: apply
  image: hashicorp/terraform:${TF_VERSION}
  script:
    - terraform init
    - terraform apply tfplan
  dependencies:
    - tf-plan        # downloads tfplan artifact from tf-plan job
  rules:
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH
      when: manual  # requires a human to click 'run'
  environment:
    name: production
    action: start
```

sections.title: Rules — control when jobs run
sections.body:
`rules` replaces the old `only`/`except` and is much more powerful.

```yaml
job-name:
  rules:
    # Condition 1: run on MRs
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
      when: always

    # Condition 2: run on main, but only if terraform files changed
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == "main"
      changes:
        - "terraform/**/*"
        - "*.tf"
      when: always

    # Condition 3: never run on tags
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_TAG
      when: never

    # Default: don't run (if no rule matched)
    - when: never

# Common CI variables for rules:
# $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE: push | merge_request_event | schedule | web | api
# $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH:   branch name (empty on MR pipelines)
# $CI_COMMIT_TAG:      tag name (empty if not a tag)
# $CI_MERGE_REQUEST_IID: MR number
# $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH:  usually 'main' or 'master'

# Practical: run apply only on main, plan on MRs
tf-plan:
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"

tf-apply:
  rules:
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH
      when: manual

# Run a cleanup job even if the pipeline failed
cleanup:
  script: ./cleanup.sh
  when: always   # runs regardless of previous job status

# Run only if a specific variable is set
deploy-to-staging:
  rules:
    - if: $DEPLOY_ENV == "staging"
```

sections.title: Caching and artifacts — the difference matters
sections.body:
**Cache:** speeds up jobs by storing things between pipeline runs (pip packages, node_modules). Not guaranteed to be present.

**Artifacts:** pass files between jobs in the same pipeline (terraform plan output, test reports). Guaranteed for dependent jobs.

```yaml
# ── Cache: Python dependencies ─────────────────────────
pip-install:
  script:
    - pip install -r requirements.txt
  cache:
    key:
      files:
        - requirements.txt  # cache key changes when this file changes
    paths:
      - .cache/pip
      - venv/
    policy: pull-push  # default: read and update cache

test:
  script:
    - pytest
  cache:
    key:
      files:
        - requirements.txt
    paths:
      - .cache/pip
      - venv/
    policy: pull  # only read, don't update (faster)

# ── Cache: per-branch (avoid cross-branch pollution) ───
job:
  cache:
    key: ${CI_COMMIT_REF_SLUG}  # one cache per branch
    paths:
      - node_modules/

# ── Artifacts: pass terraform plan between jobs ─────────
plan:
  script:
    - terraform plan -out=tfplan
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - tfplan
    expire_in: 1 hour

apply:
  script:
    - terraform apply tfplan
  dependencies:
    - plan  # explicitly download artifacts from plan
  # Or use 'needs' for DAG (parallel stages):
  # needs:
  #   - job: plan
  #     artifacts: true

# ── Artifacts: test reports (shown in MR UI) ────────────
test:
  script:
    - pytest --junitxml=report.xml
  artifacts:
    reports:
      junit: report.xml
    when: always   # upload even if tests fail
```

sections.title: Variables, secrets, and environment-specific config
sections.body:
```yaml
# Variable precedence (highest to lowest):
# 1. Triggered pipeline variables
# 2. Manual job variables (when clicking 'run')
# 3. Project/group CI/CD settings
# 4. .gitlab-ci.yml 'variables:' section

# ── Masked and protected variables ─────────────────────
# In GitLab UI: Settings → CI/CD → Variables
# - Masked: value hidden in logs (must be single line, no special chars)
# - Protected: only available on protected branches/tags
# HARBOR_PASSWORD: masked, protected
# AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: masked, protected

# ── Environment-specific variables ─────────────────────
variables:
  REGISTRY: harbor.example.com
  # Override per environment in GitLab UI:
  # AWS_ACCOUNT_ID (prod): 123456789012
  # AWS_ACCOUNT_ID (staging): 987654321098

# ── Using dotenv artifacts ─────────────────────────────
# Pass computed values between jobs
build:
  script:
    - |
      IMAGE_TAG="${CI_COMMIT_SHA:0:8}"
      echo "IMAGE_TAG=${IMAGE_TAG}" >> build.env
      echo "BUILD_TIME=$(date -u +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)" >> build.env
  artifacts:
    reports:
      dotenv: build.env   # variables available in downstream jobs

deploy:
  script:
    - echo "Deploying image tag: $IMAGE_TAG"   # from build.env
  needs:
    - job: build
      artifacts: true

# ── Useful predefined variables ─────────────────────────
# $CI_COMMIT_SHA          full git SHA
# $CI_COMMIT_SHORT_SHA    first 8 chars
# $CI_COMMIT_REF_NAME     branch or tag name
# $CI_COMMIT_REF_SLUG     URL-safe branch name (slashes → dashes)
# $CI_PROJECT_NAME        repo name
# $CI_PROJECT_PATH        group/repo
# $CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE      GitLab container registry URL for this project
# $CI_JOB_TOKEN          short-lived token for this job (registry auth etc.)
# $CI_MERGE_REQUEST_IID   MR number (only in MR pipelines)
```

sections.title: Cheat sheet
sections.body:
```yaml
# ── Structure ────────────────────────────────────
stages: [validate, plan, apply]  # sequential
default:                          # applied to all jobs
  image: alpine
  before_script: [...]
  retry: {max: 2, when: [runner_system_failure]}

# ── Job config ────────────────────────────────────
job:
  stage: validate
  image: hashicorp/terraform:1.8.0
  script: [terraform validate]
  rules:
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == "main"
    - when: never
  when: manual         # requires click to run
  allow_failure: true  # don't block pipeline if fails
  timeout: 10m

# ── Artifacts ────────────────────────────────────
artifacts:
  paths: [tfplan, dist/]
  reports:
    junit: report.xml
    dotenv: build.env
  expire_in: 1 day
  when: always

# ── Cache ────────────────────────────────────────
cache:
  key:
    files: [requirements.txt]
  paths: [.cache/pip, venv/]
  policy: pull  # or pull-push (default)

# ── Rules conditions ─────────────────────────────
$CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
$CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH
$CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == "main"
$CI_COMMIT_TAG
$MY_VAR == "value"
changes: ["terraform/**/*"]

# ── Key predefined variables ─────────────────────
$CI_COMMIT_SHA          $CI_COMMIT_SHORT_SHA
$CI_COMMIT_REF_SLUG     $CI_MERGE_REQUEST_IID
$CI_PROJECT_NAME        $CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE
$CI_JOB_TOKEN           $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH
```

sections.title: Quiz
sections.body:
**Q1.** What's the difference between `artifacts` and `cache`?

**Q2.** You have a terraform plan job and apply job. The apply job needs the plan file from the plan job. How do you pass it?

**Q3.** You want a deploy job to run only on `main`, and only when someone clicks a button. Write the `rules` and `when` configuration.

**Q4.** Your pipeline caches `node_modules`. The cache is sometimes stale. How do you tie cache invalidation to `package-lock.json` changes?

---

**Answers:**

**A1.** Artifacts are guaranteed to be passed between jobs in the same pipeline (deterministic). Cache is a performance optimisation — it may or may not be present (it's not guaranteed). Use artifacts for correctness, cache for speed.

**A2.** In the plan job: `artifacts: paths: [tfplan]`. In the apply job: `dependencies: [plan]` (or `needs: [{job: plan, artifacts: true}]`).

**A3.**
```yaml
rules:
  - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH
    when: manual
  - when: never
```

**A4.** Use `key: files: [package-lock.json]` — the cache key is derived from the file's hash, so it automatically invalidates when the file changes.

---

**Exercise:** Write a `.gitlab-ci.yml` that:

```yaml

# 1. Has stages: lint, test, build, deploy
# 2. lint runs on all MRs and main
# 3. test runs on all MRs and main, uploads JUnit report as artifact
# 4. build runs on main only, tags the image as CI_COMMIT_SHORT_SHA
# 5. deploy runs on main, manual, only after build
# 6. caches pip dependencies between runs
# Paste your answer here and discuss tradeoffs

# Starter:
stages:
  - lint
  - test
  - build
  - deploy

variables:
  IMAGE: harbor.example.com/my-app

# TODO: add your jobs
```
